title: Yuwell oxygen concentrator models explained: 8F-5A, 8F-5AW, 8F-10 and Spirit-3
description: Yuwell oxygen concentrator models compared: what 8F-3A, 8F-5A, 8F-5AW and 8F-10 mean, flow, purity, noise, alarms, upkeep and checks before you buy.
answer: Yuwell oxygen concentrator model numbers show the top flow and features. In the 8F series, 8F-5A gives up to 5 L/min at 95.5% to 87% oxygen, and a W suffix (8F-5AW) adds a nebuliser outlet. The 8F-3A tops out at 3 L/min, the 8F-10 at 10 L/min, and the Spirit-3 is a battery portable with pulse settings.
body:
Yuwell is one of the oxygen concentrator brands most often asked about by families arranging home oxygen. The model numbers look alike, so this guide explains what the numbers mean and how the main models differ. Every figure below comes from the Yuwell user manual, United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) records or published retailer specification sheets, listed under Sources.

Who makes Yuwell oxygen concentrators?

Yuwell concentrators are made by Jiangsu Yuyue Medical Equipment & Supply Co., Ltd., which lists a manufacturing address in Danyang, Jiangsu Province, China. Yuwell is the brand name printed on the machines and in the manuals.

The company has filed several models with the US FDA. The 8F-3A and 8F-5A received a 510(k) substantial equivalence decision on 28 April 2023 (K213825), the older 7F-5A and 7F-5B were cleared in 2009 (K083559), and the Spirit-3 portable unit was cleared on 5 June 2025 (K242736). These are US market decisions. They tell you the design was reviewed by one regulator, not that a unit is registered for sale in Pakistan. For the local position, read our guide to the DRAP Medical Devices Rules and check the current rule.

How does a Yuwell concentrator make oxygen?

A Yuwell concentrator pulls in room air and passes it through a molecular sieve that holds back nitrogen, so the gas that comes out is rich in oxygen. The FDA summary calls this pressure swing adsorption with a molecular sieve. Inside are a compressor, valves, sieve beds, a product tank, a flowmeter and an oxygen sensor.

The manual is clear that the machine is an oxygen supplement. It is not meant for life support and it does not monitor the patient. Yuwell tells users who depend on oxygen to keep a reserve supply, such as a cylinder, in case of a power cut or a fault.

What do the model numbers mean?

In the 8F series, the number after the dash is the highest recommended flow in litres per minute, and a W at the end means the unit has a built-in nebuliser outlet. The manual for the 8F-3A, 8F-3AW, 8F-5A and 8F-5AW shows this pattern: the 3 models reach 3 L/min, the 5 models reach 5 L/min, and only the 3AW and 5AW have the nebulising function.

The 8F-10 is listed by retailers as a 1 to 10 L/min unit. The 7F series is an older line. Spirit-3 is a battery portable that works on pulse settings, not litres per minute. Always confirm the full model code on the rating label, because one letter can change the features.

How do the main Yuwell models compare?

The table below puts the published figures side by side. Manual figures are from Yuwell; 8F-10 and Spirit-3 figures are from a European retailer's specification pages, so treat them as a starting point and confirm against the manual that ships with the unit.

8F-5A / 8F-5AW0 to 5 L/min95.5% to 87%52 dB(A)15.5 kg400 VA5AW only
8F-10 (retailer data)1 to 10 L/min95.5% to 87%55 dB(A)23.5 kg700 WNot listed
Spirit-3 portable (retailer data)Pulse settings 1 to 490% to 96%55 dB(A) or less2.4 kgBattery, mains and car adaptersNo

The 8F-5A measures about 39 cm wide, 24.5 cm deep and 50 cm high, with wheels. The 8F-10 is listed at 41 by 37.5 by 66.8 cm. For the 7F-5, retailer listings disagree on weight and purity, so ask for the manual before you decide.

What does the nebuliser outlet on the 8F-5AW do?

The nebuliser outlet on W models lets the same machine drive a nebuliser cup, so you do not need a separate compressor nebuliser. The manual gives a maximum nebulising rate of at least 0.15 mL/min for the 8F-3AW and 8F-5AW.

What goes in the cup and for how long is your doctor's decision. Yuwell's cleaning advice is to soak the cup, mouthpiece and tubing in warm water for about 15 minutes, never boil them, and dry everything before storage. Our guide on how to clean a nebulizer covers this in more detail.

What alarms and safety features do Yuwell concentrators have?

The 8F-5A family has alarms for power interruption, pressure or cycle failure, compressor failure and low oxygen concentration. Indicator lights show the oxygen level from the built-in sensor:

  • Green: oxygen concentration above 82%, normal operation.
  • Green and yellow: between 50% and 82%. The manual says call the supplier and keep backup oxygen nearby.
  • Red with a continuous alarm: below 50%, or a system fault. The unit shows LO, E1, E2, E3 or E4 and shuts down.

The compressor has overheat protection and a pressure relief valve. The manual says the machine takes about 30 minutes after switch-on to reach its most stable output.

Where should a Yuwell concentrator be placed?

Place the concentrator upright with at least 10 cm of clear space on every side, away from heaters, open flame and damp areas. The manual lists these rules:

  • No smoking in the room, and no oil, grease or petroleum products near the oxygen outlet or tubing.
  • Do not use an extension cord. If the mains voltage is unstable, Yuwell says to add a voltage stabiliser.
  • Normal operating range is 5 to 40 degrees Celsius and 15% to 90% relative humidity.
  • Full output is rated up to 1,828 metres above sea level. Above that, efficiency drops.
  • Cannula tubing should be no longer than 15.2 metres and free of kinks.

Units are sold in different voltage versions, including 220 V and 230 V at 50 Hz, so check the rating label matches your supply.

What maintenance does a Yuwell concentrator need?

Routine care is simple, but it has to be done. Clean the cabinet with a mild cleaner about once a month, wash and fully dry the air filter regularly, and fill the humidifier bottle with pure or distilled water between the minimum and maximum marks. Never run the machine without the filter or with a wet filter.

Yuwell says preventive maintenance is designed for once a year and should be done by trained service personnel, more often in dusty places. One retailer lists a filter cleaning reminder every 100 hours on the 8F-10. Ask who will service the unit locally before you buy.

Which Yuwell model suits which need?

The flow you need is set by the prescribing doctor, so start from the prescription, not the brand. A 3 L/min machine cannot supply a 5 L/min prescription, and a 10 L/min unit is larger, heavier and louder. Our guide to 5 litre vs 10 litre oxygen concentrators explains the difference, and buy or rent helps if the need is short term.

Before you order, confirm:

  1. The full model code, including any A, AW or other suffix.
  2. The voltage and frequency on the rating label.
  3. That the English user manual, filter and humidifier bottle are in the box.
  4. Written warranty terms and who services the unit.
  5. A backup oxygen source for power cuts.

faqs: What is the difference between Yuwell 8F-5A and 8F-5AW?
Both give up to 5 L/min of oxygen. The 8F-5AW adds a nebuliser outlet that can drive a nebuliser cup, according to the Yuwell manual.
How much oxygen purity does a Yuwell 8F-5A give?
The Yuwell manual lists 95.5% to 87% oxygen concentration for the 8F-5A and 8F-5AW. The exact figure depends on the flow setting.
How loud is a Yuwell oxygen concentrator?
The manual gives 52 dB(A) for the 8F-5A and 48 dB(A) for the 8F-3A. A retailer lists the 10 litre 8F-10 at 55 dB(A).
Can a Yuwell concentrator run during load shedding?
Not on its own. The 8F home models run on mains power, and Yuwell says oxygen-dependent users must keep a reserve supply such as a cylinder for power cuts.
